rationale: The candidate reads as one coherent compact mass in all four views, so it avoids the one-view-only failure. The dominant gesture is clear: a bent, slightly faceted bar-like volume with a modestly worked top. The plan appears to sit within the parcel and not simply fill the bounding box, and the mass does not visibly collide with itself across views. Programmatically, it can plausibly support neighborhood living/mixed neighborhood-use because it retains a compact enclosed primary volume with a legible upper hierarchy. The main weakness is the ground relationship: the thick blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly, with no strong carved public threshold, court, or entry seam, so the void/publicness score stays middling. The stepped/terraced quality is coherent enough to be read as a continuous mass rather than arbitrary stairs, but it is not especially compelling as sectional program logic. Overall this is a pass with a recommendation to sharpen the access-side void and public threshold while preserving the dominant bent-bar gesture.
